docs.overview:
Six small outline icons for action menus and row actions: `DeleteIcon`, `EditIcon`, `DuplicateIcon`, `PendingIcon`,
`OpenIcon` and `ReportIcon`. They share a 16x16 grid, a 1.4 stroke and round caps, and inherit `currentColor`.
whenToUse: Beside a visible text label in menus and buttons (decorative).
As the only content of an icon button, with an accessible name on the button.
whenNotToUse: As the only carrier of meaning without a name. If the icon stands alone, give it `aria-label`.
docs.contentGuidelines: Icons carry no text. Localised labels are supplied by the app next to the icon.

notes: **Decorative by default**: `aria-hidden="true"` and `focusable="false"`, so assistive technology skips it.
**Meaningful on request**: `aria-label` switches to `role="img"` with that name. Prefer labelling the surrounding button instead, so the name is announced once.
Icons inherit `currentColor`; contrast is the responsibility of the text colour they sit in (3:1 for non-text content).
Keyboard and focus behaviour belong to the enclosing control.

whenToUse: Recent changes to a workspace, a record or an account.
A feed where each entry is one event with a time.
whenNotToUse: Things that need a decision: use `AttentionList`.
The states of one obligation, with deadlines and inputs: use `StatusTimeline`.
Long histories: link to a full page or a table.

whenToUse: Headline figures that can change while visible: totals, counters, progress percentages.
whenNotToUse: Values that should not look like they are being computed (identifiers, dates, anything people copy exactly).
Numbers that change many times per second. Show them directly.

components.name: AppShell
components.summary: The application frame: sidebar, content area and the phone navigation sheet.

exports.name: AppShell
exports.description: The frame of an application: a sidebar on wide screens (expanded or a rail, with groups that open and close), and on phones a top bar, a floating bar within thumb reach and a navigation sheet. The navigation is data, so both layouts stay in step; the parts they are made of (`Sidebar`, `SidebarGroup`, `SidebarItem`, `MobileFloatBar`, `NavSheet`) are exported for apps that need another arrangement. A click on a link makes it look current at once and the sheet close; `aria-current` follows the real `currentPath`. The shell renders the page's only `<main>` and a skip link to it.

props.description: The navigation, as data. It renders in the sidebar and again in the phone sheet.

props.name: currentPath
props.description: The path being shown: the matching item is current (`aria-current="page"`).

props.name: isActive
props.description: Takes over from `currentPath`. Return true for the current item.

props.name: brand
props.description: Brand or workspace switcher, at the top of the sidebar, the sheet and the phone top bar. A function gets the rail state.

props.name: context
props.description: Between the brand and the search, in the sidebar, and above the navigation in the sheet: the workspace, company or account the person is in, and a switcher for it. A function gets the surface (see `AppShellSlotState`), so a switcher can open as a dropdown in the sidebar and inline in the sheet. Rendered once per surface, so do not give its parts a fixed `id`.

props.name: footer
props.description: Bottom of the sidebar, and of the sheet: account, help and sign-out links.

props.name: topBarEnd
props.description: Right side of the phone top bar: a workspace chip, a status.

props.name: search
props.description: A search entry in the sidebar and on the floating bar.

props.name: searchTrigger
props.description: Replaces the sidebar's search entry with your own (a function gets the rail state). The floating bar's entry still comes from `search`.

props.name: primaryAction
props.description: The main action when no page registers its own with `useShellPrimaryAction`: on the floating bar, and in any `ShellPrimaryActionSlot`.

props.name: desktopPrimaryFallback
props.description: Whether wide screens show the shell's `primaryAction` in `ShellPrimaryActionSlot` while no page has registered its own. Default `true`. Set `false` when the default makes sense only on phones (the floating bar still shows it), so a hard load never flashes an action the page is about to replace or remove.

props.name: menuData
props.description: `data-*` attributes for the floating bar's menu button.

props.name: navigationPending
props.description: Shown in place of the navigation, in the sidebar and in the sheet, while the next route loads: a skeleton. The navigation landmarks are `aria-busy` meanwhile. Leave it out when the navigation is ready.

props.name: topBar
props.description: A bar above the page, beside the sidebar, at every width: a unit or context picker.

props.name: statusRow
props.description: A row between `topBar` and the page: sync state, a notice. Give it the live-region semantics it needs.

props.name: sheetAs
props.description: `portal` (default) or a native `<dialog>` for the phone navigation sheet (`NavSheet` `renderAs`).

props.name: menuOpen
props.description: The phone navigation sheet is open. Controlled: open it from your own control (a context chip in the top bar) and hear it close through `onMenuOpenChange`. Leave it out and the menu button drives it.

props.name: hideSheetNavigation
props.description: Hide the navigation inside the phone sheet and leave the `context` slot and footer: a switcher that takes over the sheet while it is open. The sidebar is not affected.

props.name: collapsed
props.description: Sidebar as a rail. Controlled.

props.name: openGroups
props.description: Keys of the open collapsible groups. Controlled; the owner then also decides what arriving on a page opens.

props.name: fixedSidebar
props.description: Hide the rail button. Default `false`.

props.name: routeKey
props.description: Identifies the page being shown, usually the pathname. When it changes, the page inside `<main>` enters with a short fade and rise (`RouteTransition`), the route progress bar finishes, and the navigation skeleton gives way. A search-param change or a refresh keeps the key and plays nothing; neither does the first load. Nothing remounts for it. Pass the pathname, not the query string. Wrapping the page adds one element around `children`.

props.name: routePending
props.description: A navigation to another route has started and the page is not there yet: drives a thin progress bar at the top of the window. Needs `routeKey`. The bar appears only when the wait outlasts 150 ms, so fast navigations do not flash, and, unless you pass this prop, a plain click on a link to another path starts it by itself.

props.name: routeTrackLinks
props.description: Let a plain click on a link to another path start the progress bar as well, alongside `routePending`: the bar then shows while either is in progress. Default: `true` without `routePending`, `false` with it (the app drives the bar alone). Set it `true` to drive query-string navigations through `routePending` and still track link clicks. `RouteProgress` `trackLinks`.

props.name: routeTransitionProps
props.description: A class and `data-*` attributes for the region that wraps the page and plays the route motion, so an app can hook its own entrance CSS (a stagger over the page's sections) onto the `data-route-enter` its children get. Needs `routeKey`.

props.name: routeProgress
props.description: Draw the progress bar when `routeKey` is given. Default `true`.

props.name: mainPending
props.description: A skeleton shown in `<main>` in place of the page while a slow navigation loads. The page stays mounted but hidden, so its state and the providers around it survive, and `mainStart` stays visible. `<main>` is `aria-busy` meanwhile. Decide when to show it (most apps wait a few hundred milliseconds so fast navigations never flash one) and give it the shape of the page it stands in for.

props.name: floatScrim
props.description: Fade the page out behind the floating bar on phones, so content scrolling under it does not end in a hard edge. Default `false`: nothing is drawn unless asked for.

props.name: mainProps
props.description: Attributes for the `<main>` the shell owns: `id` (the skip link follows it), `className`, `data-*`, `tabIndex`, ARIA. `className` is added to the shell's own.

props.name: mainKey
props.description: Remounts the `<main>` and everything in it when it changes, as React's `key` does: a workspace or scope switch that must drop the page's state. Leave it out for a page change, which `children` handles.

props.name: mainStart
props.description: The first thing inside `<main>`, before `children`: banners that belong to the page area and scroll with it (a trial notice, a cookie or install hint). Unlike `topBar` and `statusRow`, which sit beside `<main>` and stay put, this remounts with `mainKey` and takes the page's padding.

props.description: The page. The shell renders the one `<main>` landmark around it.

exports.name: NavSheet
exports.description: A modal bottom sheet that holds the app's navigation on a phone. It rises from the bottom edge, dims the page, traps focus, closes on Escape, on a tap on the dimmed page, and on a swipe down from the grabber or header. The page behind is inert and cannot scroll. Focus lands on the sheet itself when it opens and returns to the control that opened it. Under `prefers-reduced-motion` it appears and disappears at once; dragging still follows the finger.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the dialog.

props.name: header
props.description: Next to the close button: a brand or a title.

props.name: footer
props.description: Below the scrolling body, pinned to the bottom: account and help links.

props.name: closeLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the close button. Defaults to the provider's `close` label.

props.name: swipeToDismiss
props.description: Let the grabber and header be dragged down to dismiss, and the body too while it is scrolled to the top. Default `true`.

props.name: closeOnNavigate
props.description: Close the sheet when a link inside it is followed (a plain click on an `<a href>` in the body or footer; not an open-in-new-tab click). `AppShell` turns it on so footer and slot links behave like the navigation's own. Default `false`.

props.name: container
props.description: Where the sheet is mounted. Defaults to `document.body`, so the rest of the page can be made inert.

props.name: renderAs
props.description: `portal` (default) renders a fixed-position layer in a portal, with an animated exit. `dialog` renders a native `<dialog>` opened with `showModal()`, so the sheet sits in the browser's top layer; the page behind is made inert by the browser, the backdrop is the native `::backdrop` and the exit is immediate. Focus trap, Escape, scroll lock, swipe to dismiss and the layer stack work the same in both.

exports.name: RouteProgress
exports.description: A thin progress bar fixed to the top of the window while a navigation is loading. It is a signal, not an overlay: it shows only when the wait outlasts `revealDelay`, creeps toward 85%, jumps to the end when `routeKey` changes and fades out (opacity, with the exit token). A run that is never finished ends by itself after 10 seconds. It is decorative (`aria-hidden`); announce a long wait with your own live region. Only `transform` and `opacity` move, with the motion tokens, so under reduced motion it steps without easing.

props.name: routeKey
props.description: Identifies the page being shown (the pathname). When it changes, the navigation has arrived and the bar finishes. `AppShell` passes its own `routeKey`.

props.name: pending
props.description: A navigation has started and not arrived. Set it from the router's pending state, or from your own click handler for a programmatic navigation (a query-string change the link tracking does not see). Going back to `false` without a new `routeKey` (a cancelled navigation) finishes the bar, unless a tracked link click is still on its way. When you pass it (even as `false`), link clicks stop starting the bar unless `trackLinks` is set explicitly.

props.name: trackLinks
props.description: Start on a plain click on a same-origin link that leads to another path (`<a href>`, which includes a router's links). Not for modified clicks, `target` other than `_self`, downloads, the current path or a link that only changes the query string or hash. A run started this way ends when `location.href` changes, when `routeKey` changes, or after 10 seconds, whichever comes first. Default `true` without `pending` and `false` with it; set it `true` together with `pending` and the bar shows while either is in progress.

props.name: revealDelay
props.description: Milliseconds to wait before showing the bar. Default 150.

exports.description: How an item decides that `currentPath` is its page. - `prefix` (the default): the path equals the item's or sits below it (`/settings/billing` belongs to `/settings`). - `exact`: the path equals the item's, and not the pages below it. - `query`: the path equals the item's and every query parameter in the item's `href` has the same value in `currentPath`, for sections chosen by a query string (`/admin?section=users`). Pass `currentPath` with its query. - a function: return true when `currentPath` (as you passed it, query included) is this item's page. Query strings and hashes are ignored by `prefix` and `exact`. When several items match, a function beats `query`, `query` beats a plain path, and between paths the longest wins, so two items are never current at once.

docs.overview: Columns on one zero baseline, for a weekly strip or a stack of measures per period. One scale for the whole chart, so columns compare.
whenToUse: Hovering or tapping a column should explain it (a holiday, an outlier): `interactive` with `detail`.
A short run of periods (a week, up to about twelve months) compared on one measure, or split into a few parts.
whenNotToUse: Categories with long names or exact values: use `BarList`.
A trend inside a sentence or a tile: use `Sparkline`.
Many periods, negative values or several axes: use a chart library or a table.
Nothing to show: it renders nothing, so use an `EmptyState`.

keyboard.action: Enters the columns at the last one focused (the first at first), and leaves them on the next press
Next or previous column and shows its tooltip (swapped in right-to-left)
First or last column
Dismisses the tooltip; focus stays on the column

notes: The data is a table. A visually hidden `table`, named by the `title`, lists every series as a row and every column label as a heading, so a screen reader reads the numbers; the drawing is `aria-hidden` shape on top of it, except when `interactive` is set, where the columns are exposed as named images. Write the numbers with `formatValue`.
The `figure` is named by its `title`; `titleVisibility="hidden"` keeps that name for screen readers only. A written `summary` says what the columns show.
Series are named in a visible legend (shown when there are several) and in the table, so colour never carries the meaning alone. Stacked segments are also separated by a hairline.
The draw-in is `transform` only, plays once on mount and is removed under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

Columns shrink to fit and their labels wrap, down to 320px. In `forced-colors` mode, where tones collapse to one colour, each series gets its own fill pattern (solid, diagonal stripes, dots, vertical stripes, horizontal stripes, repeating after five) in the columns and in the legend, so the legend stays matchable.
Negative and non-finite numbers are drawn as 0, but the table shows them as given (through `formatValue`), so bad data is visible rather than hidden.
Print the figures people need as text beside the chart: the drawing has no value labels, unless you set `printValues`.

`interactive`: each column is a focusable `role="img"` named `<column label>: <values> · <detail>` and announced as a "column" (`aria-roledescription`, set with `columnLabel`, so people know the arrow keys move between columns) (a series is named when there are several; a `band` adds "`bandLabel` low – high"). The tooltip repeats that text visually, so it is hidden from assistive technology and there is no `aria-describedby`; the detail would be read twice. It follows the WCAG 1.4.13 conditions: Escape dismisses it (and stops there, so a dialog around the chart stays open), the pointer can move onto it, and it stays until the pointer or focus leaves. It is at most two thirds of the plot wide and anchored to the plot edge on the outer thirds, so it does not overflow, down to 320px. It fades in on `opacity`, and not at all under `prefers-reduced-motion`. A column label that is not text names the column from the label element and its values.
`printValues`: the printed totals repeat the data table, so they are hidden from assistive technology.

`band`: counted in the scale maximum and listed in the data table, under `bandLabel` (an English default, as it is aria text; set it in your language). It is drawn as a stem with two caps; in `forced-colors` mode it uses `CanvasText`.

`pattern="hatch"`: diagonal stripes in the card colour over the series colour, in the columns and in the legend. In `forced-colors` mode every series already has its own fill pattern, which replaces the hatch.

docs.overview:
A searchable single select. The person types to narrow a list and picks one option. Options can arrive asynchronously, and
the empty and loading states are part of the component.
whenToUse: A list too long to scan (more than about fifteen options), or one where people know what they are looking for.
Data that is loaded as the person types.
whenNotToUse: A short list: use `Select` (native, with the platform's picker on phones) or `RadioGroup`.
A plain text field: use `TextInput`. Without `freeText` the box only accepts a listed option.
Several choices at once: this is a single select.
A search that opens a results page: use `SearchInput`.
docs.contentGuidelines:
Labels are the thing being chosen ("City", "Assignee"), the placeholder says how ("Search for a city"). The empty text says
what to do next ("No city matches that search. Try another name."), and the loading text names what loads. Keep option labels
short and put the secondary detail (country, e-mail, code) in the description. Do not include the description in what must be
unique to tell options apart.

notes: Option ids come from their `value` and do not change between renders, so assistive technology keeps its place when the list updates.
A visually hidden status region announces the empty and loading texts, and the result count when you pass `resultsLabel`.
A list that is empty or loading is not "expanded": there is nothing to point `aria-controls` at, so the message lives in the status region only.
The highlighted option is shown with a fill and a bar on its start edge, and in forced-colors with the system highlight.

A `required` combobox is invalid until an option is chosen, whatever text is typed: the browser refuses to submit, focuses the box and shows its own message (or `requiredMessage`). It also carries `aria-required`.
A form `reset` returns it to `defaultValue`.

It opens upward when there is little room below the box. Room is measured against the viewport and every ancestor that clips vertically (a scrollable dialog body, a table cell), taking the room they all leave, and the list is shortened to the room that is left (never under about six rem). The measure is repeated, once per frame, while the page or any container scrolls and when the window is resized; scrolling does not close the list. The list is placed inside the field and is not portaled, so a clipping parent still bounds it. A portaled list is planned as a follow-up.
Given an `id`, the input keeps it, the list is `<id>-listbox` and each option is `<id>-option-<encoded value>`: any character of the value outside `A-Za-z0-9-` is written as `_<hex code point>_`.

A file picker with a drop area. The native `<input type="file">` stays in the form, limits on type, size and count are checked
with messages you provide, and the chosen files are listed with a remove button each.
whenToUse: Attachments, documents and images that are submitted with a form, where people may have the files on their desktop.
whenNotToUse: Importing data that needs a preview and column mapping: build that flow around a plain file input.

what to do: "report.docx is not supported. Use a PDF.", "huge.pdf is larger than 5 MB.". Keep the button a verb phrase
("Choose files") and the drop text secondary ("or drop files here"), since many people will not drag.

Focus on the input draws the focus ring on the button.
Refusals use `role="alert"` and are part of the input's description. Several are shown as a list.
Each remove button is named after its file ("Remove report.pdf"; change it with `removeLabel`). After a removal focus returns to the input.
Pass `describeFiles` to have a polite status announce the new count ("2 files chosen") after a pick.
The drop area is a dashed border that fills with the accent when files are dragged over it, which is not colour alone.

The wrapper that turns a bare control into a field: a label, an optional hint, an optional error, and the wiring between
them. It generates the ids, points the label at the control, links the hint and the error with `aria-describedby`, sets
`aria-invalid` when there is an error, and marks a required field in text.
whenToUse: Every single-value control that has a label of its own: text, select, search, file, combobox.
whenNotToUse: A group of checkboxes or radios. Those have a legend, not a label: use `RadioGroup`, or a native `<fieldset>`.
A checkbox or switch on its own line. They carry their own label.
A placeholder in place of a label. A placeholder disappears as soon as the person types.

Labels are nouns, short, in sentence case: "Project name", not "Please enter the name of your project". Hints say what is
allowed or why it is asked ("Up to 40 characters"). Errors say what to do, not what went wrong: "Enter a project name to
continue", not "Invalid input". Never rely on "required" in colour; do not write "(required)" yourself, the component adds it
for assistive technology.

The control's accessible description is the hint followed by the error.
`aria-invalid="true"` is present only while there is an error, so a pristine field is not announced as invalid.
Validate on blur or on submit, not on every keystroke, so the alert does not interrupt typing.

components.summary: A dialog that interrupts the page and traps focus until it is dismissed.

exports.name: Modal
exports.description: A modal dialog in a portal. Traps focus, locks page scroll, makes the page behind inert, restores focus to the trigger on close, and enters and leaves with the package's motion (scale on larger screens, a sheet rising from the bottom on phones). Follows the WAI-ARIA APG Dialog (Modal) pattern; with `role="alertdialog"`, the Alert Dialog pattern. The panel publishes the height its sticky header covers as `--lufia-modal-header-block-size`, kept current with a `ResizeObserver`, so sticky content in the body can use `top: var(--lufia-modal-header-block-size, 0px)` instead of a hand-tuned number. It is `0px` with `scrollShadow`, where the body scrolls below the header.

props.name: onClose

A dialog that blocks the page behind it until the person answers or dismisses it. Portaled to `document.body`, with focus
containment, scroll lock, an inert background and an enter/exit motion.
whenToUse: A focused task or a decision that must be finished or abandoned before returning to the page: editing a record, picking from a list, confirming settings.
Anything that interrupts and needs an answer: build on it with [ConfirmDialog](?path=/docs/components-overlays-confirmdialog--docs).
whenNotToUse: A message that does not need a response: use a [Toast](?path=/docs/components-feedback-toast--docs).
Content the person should be able to compare with the page. A side panel or an inline expansion lets them keep the context a modal hides.
Navigation. If the content has its own URL and is more than a step, make it a page. To make a modal linkable, drive `open` with `useModalState`.
docs.contentGuidelines:
Titles say what the dialog is for ("Edit project", "Delete invoice 2041?"), not "Are you sure?". Buttons say what they do
("Save changes"), not "OK". Put the primary action last and the cancel action before it; on phones the order reverses so the
primary action sits on top.

notes: `role="dialog"` (or `alertdialog`), `aria-modal="true"`, `aria-labelledby` the title and `aria-describedby` the description when there is one.
The page behind is made `inert` and page scroll is locked, so neither keyboard, pointer nor screen reader can reach it. The notification region of `ToastProvider` stays live.
The dialog is the scroll container, with the header and footer sticky. Long content scrolls with the arrow keys while focus is on the dialog, with no extra tab stop.
Close button: 36 px on desktop and 44 px on phones. Focus is always visible. Under `forced-colors` the border uses `CanvasText`.
Motion uses `--lufia-motion-duration-enter` (240 ms) and `-exit` (160 ms), scale on desktop and rise on phones. Under `prefers-reduced-motion` it appears and disappears at once.
Choose the initial focus deliberately. The default (the dialog) is safe for informational content; for a destructive prompt focus the safe action (`ConfirmDialog` does).

exports.name: MoreActions
exports.description: An overflow menu: a button that opens a list of actions. It follows the WAI-ARIA menu button pattern, with a roving focus that arrow keys, Home, End and typeahead move through. Escape and a press outside close it through `useDismiss`, which also keeps the layer order right when the menu sits inside a dialog. As a popover the open menu is portalled out of the component (to `document.body`, or into the open modal it sits in) and placed with `position: fixed` from the trigger's box, so an ancestor with `overflow: hidden` cannot clip it. It lines up with `align` and flips to the other edge, or opens upward, when it would leave the viewport, and it follows the trigger on scroll and resize. Until the component has mounted (server render, hydration) it renders in place. As a sheet (`presentation`) the menu moves to a portal on `document.body`: a backdrop covers the viewport, focus is trapped in the sheet, the page behind is inert, and Escape or a tap on the backdrop closes it and returns focus to the button. The sheet's stacking order is `--lufia-overlay-z`, which an app raises to clear a fixed dock or bar of its own.

docs.overview:
A bell button with an unread count that opens a panel of notifications. On wide pages the panel hangs from the bell as a
non-modal popover; below 60rem it is a modal bottom sheet. The data and every string come from the caller: the package has
no i18n and no data layer.
whenToUse: A feed of things that happened or need a decision, with an unread state, reachable from anywhere in an app.
whenNotToUse: A single transient confirmation: use `Toast`.
Blocking questions: use `Modal` or `ConfirmDialog`.
A page-length activity log with no unread state: use `ActivityList`.
docs.contentGuidelines:
Titles say what happened in one line. The meta line names the source; the time is formatted for the locale by the caller.
Keep tab labels to one word and the number of tabs to four or five. The `unreadLabel` is one word ("unread").

keyboard.action: Bell | Opens or closes the panel; focus moves into the panel
Popover | Moves through the panel's controls in order; the popover stays open
Sheet | Moves through the sheet's controls, wrapping: focus stays in the sheet
Tabs | Previous / next tab, wrapping; the tab is chosen as it takes focus
Tabs | First / last tab
Row, buttons | Activates the row (and closes the panel), "Mark all as read" or the footer
Popover, sheet | Closes the panel and returns focus to the bell

notes: The bell is a button named by `label` and the count, "Notifications, 4 unread", with `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`. The visible count repeats the name and is hidden from assistive technology.

The popover is a non-modal `role="dialog"` labelled by its heading. Focus moves to it on open; Escape returns focus to the bell. The sheet is `aria-modal`, traps focus and makes the page behind inert.

Tabs follow the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern with automatic activation and one shared `tabpanel` that lists the chosen tab's items. The arrow keys mirror in right-to-left text. A row of tabs that does not fit scrolls sideways, and the edge that hides more fades.

Each group is a heading and a list. Unread rows say so in text (`unreadLabel`, read before the title), not by the dot or the tint alone. Rows are links or buttons, so the whole row is the target and is at least 3.5rem tall.
A polite live region announces changes of `unreadCount` ("Notifications, 5 unread"). It says nothing on first paint.
"Mark all as read" stays focusable and is `aria-disabled` when nothing is unread, so focus is not lost when the last one is read.
Loading is one polite status with skeleton rows; a failure is an alert.
In forced-colors mode the unread dot and the row's start edge use `Highlight`, the selected tab keeps its underline and the summary's progress segments draw with borders.

motion.notes:
Motion uses the package's tokens and primitives and only moves `transform` and `opacity`. Every piece collapses under
`prefers-reduced-motion`: the panel simply appears and disappears, and nothing is hidden.

| Moment                         | What happens                                                                                                   |
| ------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The panel opens                | It grows out of the bell's corner (scale 0.96 to 1 with a fade). A sheet slides up, as the `MoreActions` sheet |
| The panel closes               | A shorter fade and a slight shrink (`--lufia-motion-duration-exit`), then it unmounts; it is inert meanwhile   |
| The first view of the panel    | Rows rise in a short step apart, the same sequence as the `Stagger` primitive, capped at six steps             |
| A tab changes                  | The indicator slides to the tab (`useSlidingIndicator`) and the list crossfades; rows do not re-enter          |
| The unread count changes       | The bell's badge counts with `AnimatedNumber` and pops; tab and header counts flash with `ChangeHighlight`     |
| A notification arrives         | The new row enters at the top and flashes once; nothing moves for rows that were already there                 |
| "Mark all as read"             | Each unread dot scales and fades out and the row tint fades, from top to bottom, 40 ms apart                   |
| The highlight card first shows | Its progress segments fill one after another                                                                   |

Nothing animates on first paint of a closed bell, and a re-render never replays an entrance. Try it in **Interactive**: open
the panel, switch tabs, mark everything read and simulate an arrival.

docs.overview:
Short, non-blocking notifications that stack in a corner of the screen, are announced to screen readers, close by
themselves and wait while they are hovered or focused. Mount `ToastProvider` once, call `useToast()` anywhere below.
whenToUse: Confirming something the person just did that needs no decision: saved, copied, sent, restored.
Reporting a background result they might have missed: sync finished, upload failed.
Offering **Undo** right after a reversible action. It is better than a confirmation dialog.
whenNotToUse: Anything that must be answered or read before moving on: use [ConfirmDialog](?path=/docs/components-overlays-confirmdialog--docs) or an inline message. A toast disappears, so a form's validation errors do not belong in one.
Information the person will need again (instructions, a long explanation). Put it on the page.
More than one at a time for the same outcome: identical string messages are de-duplicated, and `limit` caps the stack.
docs.contentGuidelines:
One sentence, past tense for results ("Changes saved."), the object for failures ("Upload failed. Check your connection
and try again."). Say what to do after an error. Actions are a verb ("Undo", "Retry"). Never put a link that leads
somewhere in a toast that vanishes.

notes: Announcing is separate from showing. Visually hidden live regions (`role="alert"` for errors, `role="status"` for the rest) hold a text copy of each message. One pair lives in `document.body`; another is created inside each open modal `<dialog>` for as long as it is open, because the browser makes the body inert behind it. A message goes to the announcer of the topmost open dialog, or the body's, and each one exists before anything is added to it. The visible stack is a labelled `region` that moves into the topmost dialog and back. Errors interrupt, the rest wait.

The announcer regions keep `role="alert"` and `role="status"` while empty, on purpose. A live region only announces content added after it exists, so both must be mounted first. `aria-live` alone is meant to be enough, but the explicit role is what the screen reader and browser pairs we know of announce most reliably (older VoiceOver and JAWS builds are the usual failures with a bare `aria-live`), and `role="alert"` is what marks the assertive region as errors. An empty live region is not read out, so the node costs nothing to users. We kept the roles rather than risk a silent toast.

In tests the copy means `getByText` can find the message twice. Assert what is announced with `getByRole("status")` (`"alert"` for errors) and query the visible toast inside the `Notifications` region.
Keyboard: toasts are reached in DOM order with Tab; each has its action (if any) and a dismiss button. Escape on a focused toast dismisses it. While a toast has focus its timer is paused.

The notification region stays live while a [Modal](?path=/docs/components-overlays-modal--docs) is open (the modal marks the rest of the page `inert`, except `data-lufia-inert-exempt`), though Tab cycles only inside the modal while it is open.
Targets: the dismiss button and action are at least 28 px tall (WCAG 2.5.8 asks for 24 px).

Motion: enter 240 ms and exit 160 ms, `transform` and `opacity` only, direction follows the placement. Under `prefers-reduced-motion` toasts appear and disappear at once. The success check (`SuccessCheck`) stops drawing.
Colour is never the only signal: each tone has its own icon, and the message says what happened. Under `forced-colors` the border uses system colours.
Not recorded yet: a manual VoiceOver and NVDA pass (required before `stable`).

motion.notes:
| Toast                         | Closes by itself?                                       |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `info`, `success`, `warning`  | After `duration` (5 s).                                 |
| `error`                       | Never, unless `duration` says so.                       |
| Any toast with an `action`    | Never, unless `duration` says so.                       |
| Any toast, hovered or focused | Paused; resumes with at least 1.5 s left when released. |

This follows WCAG 2.2.1 (Timing Adjustable): errors carry the most important and often the longest text, and an action
needs time to be found.

exports.description: Slides a decorative indicator behind the active item of `container`. Only `transform` animates; the items themselves never move, so their markup, focus and state are untouched. - `container` must be `position: relative`; the indicator is `position: absolute` at its top-left corner. Positions are measured physical coordinates, so the indicator uses `left: 0` rather than a logical inset. - `activeSelector` finds the active item inside the container. `key` re-measures when it changes (usually the active id). - The indicator starts `hidden` (server render, no script): the active item keeps its own styling until the hook shows the indicator, and CSS can hand the chrome over with `:has(> .indicator:not([hidden]))`. - The slide is enabled by `data-ready` after the first position, so the indicator never glides in from the corner. A resize jumps to the new spot instead of sliding, which would leave it at the old layout's offset for a moment. Returns the ref to put on the indicator element. Give the indicator a `transition` on `transform` under `[data-ready]`, with `--lufia-motion-*` tokens.
exports.signature: (container: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>, activeSelector: string, key: unknown, { stretch }?: UseSlidingIndicatorOptions): RefObject<HTMLSpanElement | null>

docs.overview: Slides a decorative indicator behind the active item of a tab-like row. Only `transform` animates; the items never move.
whenToUse: A small row of peer items where the chosen one should feel like it moved, not like it was swapped.
whenNotToUse: Lists that wrap onto several lines or scroll in both axes: the indicator follows one box.

notes: The indicator is decorative: give it `aria-hidden="true"`. State stays on the items (`aria-current`, `aria-pressed`).
It starts `hidden`, so with no script or before the first measure the active item keeps its own styling.

The slide is switched on one frame after the first position, so it never glides in from the corner. A resize jumps instead of sliding. Under `prefers-reduced-motion` the duration tokens collapse and the indicator simply appears in place.
Positions are measured, physical coordinates; the indicator uses `left: 0` on purpose and follows the items in RTL layouts too.

exports.name: useStepDirection
exports.description: Which way a multi-step flow just moved: `"next"` when `step` increased, `"back"` when it decreased, `undefined` until the first change (so opening a wizard never plays a slide) and again once the flow is no longer `active`. Render it as `data-step-direction` on the step container and let CSS slide the new step in from that side: forward comes from the right, back from the left.

docs.overview: Tells a multi-step flow which way it just moved, so the new step can slide in from the matching side.
whenToUse: Wizards and stepped dialogs, where direction helps people keep their place ("one direction language": forward is right, back is left).
whenNotToUse: Tabs or other non-linear navigation, where there is no forward.

notes: The hook only returns a value; it moves nothing. Keep the keyframes `from`-only and driven by `--lufia-motion-*` tokens so they collapse under `prefers-reduced-motion` (see Motion).
The direction must never be the only signal of the new step: announce it (`Stepper` does) and keep the heading current.
Opening the flow returns `undefined`, so a wizard never slides on first paint.
